Source: Kochhar, Rakesh, and Anthony Cilluffo. "How Wealth Inequality Has Changed in the U.S. since the Great Recession, by Race, Ethnicity and Income." Pew Research Center. Nov 1, 2017.
DATA:
- Y-axis: Median household net worth ($) from 0 to 900K in increments of 100K.
- X-axis categories and years:
  - Lower income:
    - 2007: ≈ 18K
    - 2013: ≈ 9K
    - 2016: ≈ 10K
  - Middle income:
    - 2007: ≈ 164K
    - 2013: ≈ 101K
    - 2016: ≈ 110K
  - Upper income:
    - 2007: ≈ 740K
    - 2013: ≈ 660K
    - 2016: ≈ 810K
KEY FACTS:
- Upper-income households have significantly higher median net worth than lower- and middle-income households across all years shown (2007, 2013, and 2016).
- For all three income groups, median household net worth dropped between 2007 and 2013 following the Great Recession.
- Upper-income households experienced a strong recovery and growth by 2016, surpassing their 2007 levels.
- Lower- and middle-income households saw partial or minimal recovery by 2016, remaining well below their 2007 pre-recession levels.
